title: Daclatasvir
overview: Daclastasvir is no longer available in the United States.

sections.Before taking daclatasvir,: tell your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to daclatasvir, any other medications, or any of the ingredients in daclatasvir tablets. Ask your pharmacist for a list of the ingredients.some medications should not be taken with daclatasvir. Other medications may cause dosing changes or extra monitoring when taken with daclatasvir. Make sure you have discussed any medications you are currently taking or plan to take before starting daclatasvir with your doctor and pharmacist. Before starting, stopping, or changing any medications while taking daclatasvir, please get the advice of your doctor or pharmacist.the following herbal product may interact with daclatasvir: St. John's wort. Be sure to let your doctor and pharmacist know that you are taking this medication before you start taking daclatasvir. Do not start this medication while taking daclatasvir without discussing with your healthcare provider. tell your doctor if you have had a liver transplant, any type of liver disease other than hepatitis C, or heart disease.tell your doctor if you are pregnant, plan to become pregnant, or are breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking daclatasvir, call your doctor.
sections.Some side effects can be serious. If you: near fainting or faintingdizziness or lightheadednessweakness or not feeling wellshortness of breathchest painmemory problemsconfusionDaclatasvir may cause other side effects. Call your doctor if you have any unusual problems while taking this medication.If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may send a report to the Food and Drug Administration's (FDA) MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online (https://www.fda.gov/Safety/MedWatch) or by phone (1-800-332-1088).
